cands.name: Sarah Crawford
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 66 (Wake County) since 2023. Served in the NC Senate, District 18, 2021–2023. CEO of the Tammy Lynn Center for Developmental Disabilities, former national director at Single Stop, and owner of Willow Strategies. NC State graduate (B.A., 2003).

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina (2026 recommendation, per Ballotpedia)

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or when she first lived in North Carolina; only her upbringing in Wake County is documented. We found no documented statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, policing and public order, or gun laws. Her campaign site does not mention school vouchers or charters. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, so no questionnaire answers were available. The sponsored-bills table on Ballotpedia did not load, so her bills are not listed. Her ownership of Willow Strategies appears only on Ballotpedia.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she was raised in Wake County and attended East Wake Middle and High School; her birthplace is not given in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the NC Senate (2021–2023) and the NC House (2023–present). Before that she was a nonprofit executive (CEO of Tammy Lynn Center, national director at Single Stop) and owned the consulting firm Willow Strategies.
qual.why: She has several years of prior legislative service in both chambers, plus a career of nonprofit executive and program and partnership leadership. Committee assignments were not counted.
qual.label: She has several years of prior legislative service in both chambers, plus a career of nonprofit executive and program and partnership leadership. Committee assignments were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she has consistently voted for access to safe, legal abortion and voted against all Republican-sponsored bills limiting abortion that came before the Senate. This is her own description of her votes, not a roll call.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she would raise teacher pay and reduce class size, and it calls for investing in public classrooms. It does not state a position on vouchers, charters or school choice.
